correctness.rationale: In the inradius-one regular 4n-gon, the polygonal norm N and Euclidean norm satisfy N(z)<=|z|_2<=sec(alpha)N(z). For every J_4-admissible pair, the smaller polygonal chord is at most the smaller Euclidean chord, which by the parallelogram identity is at most sqrt(|x|_2^2+|y|_2^2), hence at most sqrt(2)sec(alpha). For sharpness, take orthogonal unit-ball vertices u=sec(alpha)e_alpha and v=sec(alpha)e_{alpha+pi/2}, set t=tan(alpha), and rescale by c=sqrt(2/(1+t^2)). Then u+tv and u-tv lie exactly on adjacent facet-normal rays with Euclidean length sec(alpha)^2, so both polygonal chord norms equal sqrt(2)sec(alpha). The asymptotic follows from the Taylor expansion of secant.
risks: The theorem relies on the regular polygon being normalized by inradius one; other displayed normalizations must be linearly rescaled before using the coordinates.
The checker samples finitely many polygons and pairs and is not used as proof of the infinite statement.

value.rationale: The result converts an isolated octagonal evaluation into a closed formula for an infinite canonical family. The proof exposes a structural mechanism: Euclidean distortion gives the exact upper envelope, while an unequal-radius orthogonal-vertex pair with intrinsic ratio tan(pi/(4n)) simultaneously saturates the two chord norms. This identifies how the extended James domain interacts with polygonal anisotropy, gives the exact square-to-Hilbert decay and its n^{-2} rate, and supplies a reusable benchmark for comparisons with ordinary James and smoothness-based bounds.
risks: The family is restricted to side counts divisible by four; the 4n+2 case may have a different phase structure.
